lines: Here, {gift_item}. The right tool in the right hand saves a lot of trouble.
Take {gift_item}. Keep it useful and it will repay you twice.
I would rather put {gift_item} in good hands than leave it on a shelf.
Here is {gift_item}. You earned more than a quick thank-you.

I saved {gift_item} for someone who would actually use it.
This {gift_item} is yours. Fair help deserves fair thanks.
Take {gift_item} before I find another chore for it.
I hope {gift_item} makes the next hard day easier.
The village remembers who helps. Today it remembers with {gift_item}.
I cleaned up {gift_item} before bringing it over.

Keep {gift_item}. You have done enough for this village.

{gift_item} is still sitting in the best spot in {tested_villager}'s home.

{tested_villager} thanked you again after you left.

I would trust your judgment on {tested_villager} next time.

{gift_item} was not a good fit. {alternative_gift} should go over better.
{gift_subject} did not care for {gift_item}. I am sorry about that.
Leave {gift_item} off the list next time and bring {alternative_gift}.
My advice missed the mark. {gift_subject} would prefer {alternative_gift}.
Keep {gift_item} for someone else. It was wasted on {gift_subject}.

{gift_subject} tried to be polite, but the disappointment showed.

If you want to try again, start with {alternative_gift}.

Do not press {gift_subject} to like {gift_item}. Choose something else.

The gift was thoughtful even if {gift_item} was the wrong choice.
Give {gift_subject} a little time before offering {alternative_gift}.

Next time I advise you about {gift_subject}, remind me I got this one wrong.

{gift_item} did not suit them. Try {alternative_gift}.

Cross {gift_item} off the list.

Set {gift_item} aside before it causes another argument.

Do not blame my advice for ignoring their reaction.
They have different tastes than you assumed.
Take the refusal cleanly and move on.
Save {gift_item} for somebody who asks for it.

If they agree to another try, choose {alternative_gift}.

{gift_item} was obviously the wrong gift.
Do not bring them another gift until they ask.
Put {gift_item} away. You have done enough.

Stop treating them like a problem to solve.

Leave them alone until the anger passes.
No more gifts. Learn to hear a refusal.
